itens.titulo: Bank of America posts third-quarter profit drop due to $1.2 billion Treasury fine
itens.descricao: Bank of America posts third-quarter profit drop due to $1.2 billion Treasury fine CNBC
trechos: Bank of America posted a sharp decline to third-quarter profit after being hit with a $1.2 billion penalty by the U.S.
Shares of the bank fell more than 4% in premarket trading.

Here's what the company reported: - Earnings per share: 91 cents, may not compare with $1.10 LSEG estimate - Revenue: $30.12 billion vs. $30.69 billion estimate The bank's profit fell 17% to $6.93 billion, or 91 cents a share.
Excluding the penalty, which sapped income by 17 cents, EPS would've been $1.08 a share.
Revenue rose 3.2% to $30.12 billion in the quarter, below expectations by about $570 million, largely on misses from Wall Street trading operations.
Fixed income trading revenue fell 17% to $2.55 billion on weakness in mortgages, municipals, and credit activity.
That is roughly $450 million below the StreetAccount estimate.
Equities trading revenue climbed 10% to $2.51 billion, but that was also below analysts' expectations, by nearly $300 million.

itens.titulo: Bank of America Heads Into Q3 Earnings Carrying a $1.2 Billion Treasury Penalty
itens.descricao: Bank of America Heads Into Q3 Earnings Carrying a $1.2 Billion Treasury Penalty Yahoo Finance
trechos: Bank of America received a $1.2 billion bill from the US Treasury a day before its earnings report.
On Tuesday, the Treasury hit the second-largest US bank with more than $1.21 billion in anti-money-laundering and sanctions penalties.
The bank said the charge will cut third-quarter net income by about 17 cents per share.
A $1.2 Billion Bill Lands on the Eve of Bank of America's Q3 Earnings The penalties total more than $1.21 billion and come from three Treasury agencies.
- $1.2 billion from FinCEN: The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network's penalty is the third-largest in Treasury history.
- $750 million from the OCC: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency imposed its largest penalty ever, counted within FinCEN's figure.
- $11.66 million from OFAC: The Office of Foreign Assets Control settled separately over 475 apparent sanctions violations.
Treasury said the bank failed to report more than $5 billion in suspicious transactions on time.

itens.titulo: Bank of America Q3 profit tumbles 17% as fines, Wall Street slowdown dent lending income
itens.descricao: Bank of America Q3 profit tumbles 17% as fines, Wall Street slowdown dent lending income Yahoo Finance
trechos: Bank of America said Wednesday that its third quarter profit fell 17% from a year earlier as $1.2 billion regulatory penalty and a slowdown in its Wall Street machine dented higher lending income.
Bank of America's (BAC) stock fell more than 3% in premarket trading.
The nation's second biggest bank reported Q3 net income of $6.93 billion, or $0.91 per share, compared with the $1.10 per share analysts expected.
"Excluding the regulatory penalty, Bank of America said it earned $8.1 billion, or $1.08 per share, with adjusted earnings per share rising 4% from a year earlier.
Revenue rose 3% to $30 billion, compared with expectations of roughly $30.6 billion.
"While investment banking and sales and trading revenues were lower, commercial lending grew in every client segment," Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan said in a statement with the release.
"Our momentum, reflected in growth in client deposits, wealth flows and consumer activity, supported solid earnings, balance-sheet growth and long-term shareholder value," he added.
Bank of America's net interest income, a core measure for what the bank earns from lending, rose 8% from a year earlier to $16.4 billion, supported by higher loan and deposit balances.

itens.titulo: Bitcoin ETFs Just Had Their Best Day of October While XRP ETFs See No Inflows for Three Sessions. Are Investors Rotating to BTC?
itens.descricao: Bitcoin ETFs Just Had Their Best Day of October While XRP ETFs See No Inflows for Three Sessions. Are Investors Rotating to BTC? Yahoo Finance
trechos: Quick Read - Bitcoin ETFs pulled in $176M on October 13, their best single day this month, yet October still sits at a net $278M outflow overall.
- XRP ETFs logged zero net flow for three straight sessions, with trading volume hitting a monthly low of $20.5M, signaling fading investor interest.
(Sponsor) Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) spot exchange-traded funds (ETFs) saw an impressive $175.6 million inflow, one of the month's largest increases, according to SoSoValue.
This surge followed a $65.4 million outflow the previous session, making October 13 the second-biggest inflow day this month.
Currently, Bitcoin is trading at $83,382, flat on the day after moving between $82,919 and $84,025.
Over the past week, it's down 0.9%, but it's up 7.1% over the last 30 days.
Meanwhile, XRP is priced at $1.37, down 6.9% for the week.
